earlier_scan.note: Long-extinct; only 18th-c. wordlists (Steller/Krasheninnikov); Georg & Volodin 1999 grammar is Western Itelmen

sources.citation: Bogoras, Waldemar. 1922. Chukchee. In Franz Boas (ed.), Handbook of American Indian Languages, Part 2 (BAE Bulletin 40), 631-903. Washington: GPO.
sources.note: p. 641: 'In Krasheninnikoff's time there were three dialects of the Kamchadal - a southern, an eastern.., and a western. The first two are extinct'. §24 Accent (pp. 680-681): 'In all three languages the accent usually recedes to the beginning of the word, even as far as the fourth or fifth syllable from the end' (example Kamchadal klta'tilkajuknan); emphasis may throw accent to the last syllable. This concerns Western Kamchadal (Khairyuzovo/Sedanka), not the southern dialect.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page sout3274 'South Itelmen' (alt. name East Itelmen, NOCODE_East-Itelmen).
sources.note: No descriptive references listed; subclassification comment cites Worth 1961: 595-596 and Georg & Volodin 1999: 216-224. Extinct.

sources.citation: [unsigned]. n.d. (c. 2022-2025). Itel'menskij jazyk [The Itelmen language]. In: Interaktivnyj atlas korennyx malochislennyx narodov Severa, Sibiri i Dal'nego Vostoka Rossijskoj Federacii: jazyki i kul'tury. Moskva: Institut jazykoznanija RAN (atlaskmns.ru).
sources.note: Says the northern and southern Itelmen languages died out at the end of the 19th - beginning of the 20th c; gives a few words per variety; the phonetics section describes modern (western) Itelmen consonants and vowels only; the word 'udarenie' does not occur on the page. No statement.

sources.citation: Volodin, A. P. (comp.), Ch. Ono (ed.), J. Bobaljik, D. Koester, M. Krauss. 2021. Polnyi itel'mensko-russkii slovar'. St Petersburg / Fuerstenberg: Kulturstiftung Sibirien (SEC). Section 'Iuzhnoitel'mensko-russkii slovar'' pp. 345-350 (from Krasheninnikov 'Krsh_Yu' and Dybowski 'Dyb_Yu').
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the southern entries are re-spelled without accent marks (e.g. 'аатт Ю. постель <Крш_Ю>'). Preface: Krasheninnikov distinguished three 'narechiia' (eastern, southern, western; 155-item list); Dybowski (1878-83) still found all three alive, the southern in critical state (shortest list); Tiushov (1890s) found the southern already gone.

sources.citation: Institut jazykoznanija RAN, Laboratorija issledovanija i soxranenija malyx jazykov. 2019-2026. Itel'menskij jazyk. In: Malye jazyki Rossii (web encyclopedia, minlang.iling-ran.ru).
sources.note: States that the peculiarities of the southern and eastern Itelmen languages were phonetic innovations (development of voiced stops), that 200-word lists of the three Itelmen languages were recorded by the Billings expedition (1791) and by Dybowski (1870s); the phonetics section (consonant inventory, ejectives, clusters) has nothing on stress. No statement.

sources.citation: Duerr, Michael. 2013. Die Erforschung der Sprachen Kamchatkas. In E. Kasten (ed.), Reisen an den Rand des Russischen Reiches, 287-296. Fuerstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Krasheninnikov (1755) published 161 words in three Itelmen varieties in list form, that Steller's 1774 book has no separate Itelmen lists (they were lost), and that Radloff 1861 notes many errors in Krasheninnikov's printed lists.

sources.citation: Steller, Georg Wilhelm. 2013 [1774]. Beschreibung von dem Lande Kamtschatka. Herausgegeben von Erich Kasten und Michael Dürr (Bibliotheca Kamtschatica). Fürstenberg/Havel: Verlag der Kulturstiftung Sibirien. 280 pp.
sources.note: Ethnographic: three Itelmen 'Haupt-Dialectos' and impressionistic articulation remarks only ('so bleibt die itelmenische halb in dem Hals und Mund stecken.. wird leise und mit vielen Ziehen, Dehnen und Torturen.. ausgesprochen', p. 21); editors' preface notes Itelmen words were rendered inadequately and need study against Steller's manuscript 'Specimen linguarum'; no accent/stress statement; no separate Itelmen wordlist in the printed work.

sources.citation: Mudrak, Oleg A. 2008. Kamchukchee and Eskimo glottochronology and some Altaic etymologies found in the Swadesh list. Aspects of Comparative Linguistics 3 (Orientalia et Classica XIX), 297-336. Moscow: RSUH.
sources.note: No Kamchadal phonology; the only 'accentuation' remark concerns Proto-Eskimo vowel reduction. Not kept held by the project (checked and deleted).

sources.citation: [IEA RAN]. c. 2005. Itel'menskij jazyk. In: Jazyki narodov Sibiri, naxodjashchiesja pod ugrozoj ischeznovenija [Endangered languages of the peoples of Siberia] (web survey, Institut etnologii i antropologii RAN, lingsib.iea.ras.ru).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/historical survey: c. 1700 three mutually intelligible dialects (western, eastern, southern); Krasheninnikov's c. 200 words in all three; modern Itelmen = former western dialect. No phonology at all; no statement.

sources.citation: Jarceva, V. N. (gl. red.). 1990. Lingvisticheskij enciklopedicheskij slovar'. Moskva: Sovetskaja enciklopedija. Entries: Krejnovich, E. A. 'Omokskij jazyk'; Volodin, A. P. 'Itel'menskij jazyk'; [unsigned] 'Jukagiro-chuvanskie jazyki' (online transcription tapemark.narod.ru/les).
sources.note: High consonant saturation, no incorporation, nominative syntax; nothing on stress. No statement.

sources.citation: Bogoraz, V. G. 1934. Itel'menskii (kamchadal'skii) iazyk. In Iazyki i pis'mennost' narodov Severa, ch. III, 85-. Leningrad.
sources.note: §2: only the Sedanka (northern) and Khairyuzovo (southern) dialects of Western Itelmen survive. §13 (p. 89): 'Ударение в ительменском так же как в луораветланском и нымыланском, падает на начало слова, чаще всего на первый или второй слог' - Western Itelmen only. §14 mentions Dybowski's materials 'collected in the south of Kamchatka' for plural suffixes -t, -da; nothing on southern stress.

sources.citation: Radliński, Ignacy. 1892. Słowniki narzeczy ludów kamczackich. III. Słownik narzecza Kamczadałów południowych. Ze zbiorów Prof. B. Dybowskiego. Kraków: Nakładem Akademii Umiejętności (osobne odbicie z t. XVII Rozpraw Wydziału filologicznego AU), 22 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content: title page then an alphabetical Polish/Latin glossary with Dybowski's Russian-Cyrillic spellings in parentheses; the Cyrillic and Latin forms carry no accent marks (page scan of p. [104] checked); no preface in this part.

sources.citation: Radliński, Ignacy. 1891. Słowniki narzeczy ludów kamczackich. I. Słownik narzecza Ainów, zamieszkujących wyspę Szumszu.. ze zbiorów Prof. B. Dybowskiego [series introduction, pp. 1-2]. Kraków: AU (odbitka z Rozpraw Wydz. filol. t. XVI).
sources.note: Describes how Dybowski elicited Russian word lists in Cyrillic ('w transkrypcyi rosyjskiej, pismem grażdańskiem') and Radliński's Latin transliteration rules (palatalisation diacritic, č š ž); explicitly warns 'Ułożone na ich podstawie słowniki mogą być pod wielu względami niedokładne, zwłaszcza pod fonetycznym i etymologicznym'; no mention of accent/stress marking.

sources.citation: Sauer, Martin. 1802. An account of a geographical and astronomical expedition to the northern parts of Russia.. performed.. by Commodore Joseph Billings, in the years 1785, &c. to 1794. London: T. Cadell, jun. & W. Davies. Appendix I 'Vocabulary of the Yukagir, Yakut, and Tungoose (or Lamut) languages'; Appendix II 'Vocabulary of the languages of Kamtshatka, the Aleutan Islands, and of Kadiak'.
sources.note: Wordlist in English-based spelling without accent marks; only remark: 'There are many words in the Language of Kamtshatka that I was not able to pronounce.. which is the cause of so many blanks' and (p. 308) 'nor is their language pure'. No statement; no marks.

sources.citation: Lesseps, Jean-Baptiste-Barthelemy de. 1790. Travels in Kamtschatka, during the years 1787 and 1788. Translated from the French [Journal historique du voyage de M. de Lesseps, Paris 1790]. 2 vols. London: J. Johnson. Vol. 2, pp. 383-403 'Vocabulary of the Kamtschadale, Koriac, Tchouktchi, and Lamout languages'; pp. 404 ff. 'Vocabulary of the Kamtschadale language at St. Peter and St. Pauls, and at Paratounka'; vol. 1, p. 146 'Idiom' (Bolcheretsk) and Preface (pronunciation of the transcription).
sources.note: Wordlists in French-based spelling with occasional acute e (French orthography, not stress marks). Vol. 2 note: 'Though the language at Bolcheretsk be different from what is spoken at both these places, all the words of this Vocabulary are there made use of.' Vol. 1 p. 146: 'The Kamtschadale idiom appeared to me to be uncouth, guttural, and difficult to be pronounced; the words are broken, and the sounds disagreeable. There are as many different dialects and accents as there are ostrogs. For instance, upon leaving Saint Peter and Saint Paul, we are astonished to hear a different jargon at Par…

sources.citation: Steller, Georg Wilhelm. 1774. Beschreibung von dem Lande Kamtschatka. Frankfurt/Leipzig: Fleischer.
sources.note: Fraktur scanned is largely unusable; per Duerr 2013 the printed edition contains no separate Itelmen wordlists (only a Koryak vocabulary and scattered words). Nothing on stress found.

sources.citation: Krasheninnikov, S. P. 1755. Opisanie zemli Kamchatki, tom 2, Chast' 3, gl. 11 'O razlichnykh narechiiakh Kamchatskogo naroda', pp. 137-145 (comparative wordlist of three Kamchadal dialects pp. 138-144, column b = southern; Lord's Prayer in southern Kamchadal from Steller's notes p. 145). SPb: Imp. Akademiia nauk.
sources.note: No statement about stress anywhere. But the wordlist (all three columns, incl. the southern column b) and the southern Lord's Prayer are printed with acute accent marks on one vowel per word, e.g. southern 'Ку́тхай' god, 'Ка́на' devil, 'Ко́халъ' sky, 'Чкуа́да' legs, 'Пайма́нъ' stockings, 'Танга́къ' fur coat, 'Та́ша' fort, 'Куа́шуа' axe, 'Кусга́лъ' day, 'Ку́лкуа' night (pp. 138, 141, viewed on page scan). Accents fall on first, second or final syllables with no obvious pattern; the only prose remark on pronunciation concerns the letter 'г с палочкою на верху' to be pronounced like Latin g (p.…

sources.citation: Mudrak, O. A. (comp.). n.d. Itelmen etymology [Itel'menskaja etimologija], database 'itelet' of the Chukchee-Kamchatkan etymological databases, The Tower of Babel / Starling project (S. A. Starostin et al.), 1670 records with Proto-Itelmen, West Itelmen and South Itelmen fields.
sources.note: Lexical database: proto-forms and attested West/South Itelmen forms with glosses and comments; no description of stress; apostrophes mark glottal stops, not accent. Forms only, no statement.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; ru bibliography lists Mudrak 2008 'Svod kamchadal'skoi leksiki po pamiatnikam XVIII veka', Dybowski 1998 'Slovar' itel'menskogo iazyka' (Warszawa: Energeia), Radlinski 1891-94, Georg & Volodin 1999, Fortescue 2005.

tone.quote: К сожалению, поскольку мы не имеем текстовых материалов на вымерших восточно- и южнокамчадальском языках и вынуждены довольствоваться лишь списками лексики, мы не можем делать выводов о грамматическом устройстве этих языков и их отличиях от западнокамчадальского. [...] Как мы упоминали выше, по южно- и восточнокамчадальскому языкам не существует текстовых материалов, так же отсутствуют аудио- и видеозаписи. Единственные доступные языковые материалы – списки лексики
tone.locator: sec. II.4 'Osnovnye lingvisticheskie svedenija (fonetika, grammatika, leksika)', first paragraph; sec. III 'Illjustrativnye materialy', first paragraph
tone.translation: Unfortunately, since we have no text material in the extinct East and South Kamchadal languages and must content ourselves with word lists only, we cannot draw conclusions about the grammatical structure of these languages and their differences from West Kamchadal. [...] As mentioned above, no text materials exist for South and East Kamchadal, and audio and video recordings are likewise absent. The only available language materials are word lists.
